Soft pneumatic arm · RAS 556 · make_calibrated_sim

Controller Study Guide

Every model and controller in the repository, derived step by step, mapped to its code, and benchmarked on one common set of tests. Repository: soft-pneumatic-arm-control, main at 3a8325c. Results: uv run python scripts/benchmark_unified.py --workers 10 (156 runs, 2 min 45 s).

Plant

make_calibrated_sim(control_hz=100, seed=s) (package soft-robotic-arm 0.4.2), fitted by the lab to 36 hardware runs. Treated as the real robot: controllers read only the tip (\(\xi\), motion capture), the tip velocity, and the pressure sensors.

  • Inputs: \(P^{\text{cmd}}_{S2}, P^{\text{cmd}}_{S3}, P^{\text{cmd}}_{S4}\), 0–9 psi. \(S_1\) is a sealed reservoir (2 psi charge), not commandable.
  • Actuator per segment: regulator gain and bias, 0.5 s dead time, 0.6 s first-order lag. Identified gains \(G = (1.12, 1.10, 1.16)\), biases \((0.45, 0.15, 0.30)\) psi.
  • Raising \(S_2\) moves the tip toward \(+y\), \(S_3\) toward \(-x\), \(S_4\) toward \(-y\) (step tests, docs/log.md). x has one segment, y has two opposing segments.
  • Reach with 0–9 psi: about ±9 mm in x, ±19 mm in y (static); about ±4.8 mm at 0.4 Hz (benchmark_slide_tasks.json, reach_checks).
  • The scored task: CircularTrackingTask(), 7 mm circle at 0.1 Hz, 5 s settle at 4.5 psi, 30 s tracked, starts 7 mm from \(\xi_0\).

Models

One-mode model (Nikoletta's notebook)

1Five-link chain, one bending plane

\[ M\ddot\theta + D\dot\theta + K\theta = g\,\mathbf 1\,\Delta p,\qquad K = k_\theta I,\ D = d_\theta I \]

\(\theta\in\mathbb R^5\): hinge angles of the simulator's chain; \(M\) from MuJoCo (mj_fullM); \(k_\theta = 0.4168\) N·m/rad, \(d_\theta = 0.3629\) N·m·s/rad; \(g = 3.567\cdot10^{-3}\) N·m/psi; gravity and actuator omitted. smc_reduced_model.py:47-63

2Modes

\[ K v_r = \omega_r^2 M v_r,\qquad \theta = \textstyle\sum_r v_r\,\psi_r \]

\(\psi_r\): amplitude of mode \(r\). \(D = (d_\theta/k_\theta)K\), so the modes decouple exactly. Keep the mode with the largest static tip gain (mode 0, 0.52 Hz). smc_reduced_model.py:76-100

3Project onto the tip

\[ \ddot y + c_n\dot y + k_n y = b_n\,\Delta p,\qquad k_n = \omega_0^2 = 10.60\ \text{s}^{-2},\ c_n = 9.231\ \text{s}^{-1},\ b_n = -0.0820\ \tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2\text{psi}} \]

\(y\) in metres here; \(b_n = (L\cdot v_0)\,g\,(v_0\cdot\mathbf 1)\), \(L\): lever arms \(\partial\xi_x/\partial\theta\). Same constants for x and y. Parameters come from the simulator's internals, not from data. With the corrected allocator \(b_n \to +0.0820\).

M1: the paper's first-order model

1Qiao, Tao & Zhang (2024), eq. 2, in task space

\[ c_i(\rho_i)\,\dot y_i + k_i(\rho_i)\,y_i = (G_1 u)_i \;\Leftrightarrow\; \dot y_i = -a_i y_i + b_i (G_1u)_i,\quad a_i = \tfrac{k_i}{c_i},\ b_i = \tfrac{1}{c_i} \]

Inertia, gravity, actuator dynamics and delay are lumped into the paper's disturbance \(d\) (not modelled). \(\rho_x = p_{S1} - p_{S3}\), \(\rho_y = p_{S2} - p_{S4}\), \(\rho_z = \sum p\): measured scheduling variables. ndosmc.py:51-126

2Identified values

\[ G_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1.983 & -0.002\\ 2.026 & 0.001 & -2.106\\ -0.551 & -0.484 & -0.570 \end{pmatrix},\quad k \approx (0.930, 0.924, 0.942),\ c \approx (1.335, 1.338, 1.165)\ \text{s} \]

Columns of \(G_1\): \(S_2, S_3, S_4\); rows x, y, z; mm/psi. So \(a \approx 0.70\ \text{s}^{-1}\): one slow pole that stands in for delay + lag + mechanics.

M2: actuator + first-order mechanics

1Actuator (dead time + lag)

\[ \tau\,\dot p_j(t) = -p_j(t) + G_j\,u_j(t - T) \]

Standard first-order pressure model (Best et al. 2016; PneuDrive §II-B1) plus the measured dead time. ndosmc.py:78-84

2Mechanics (single constant-curvature arc, linearised, then identified)

\[ \dot y_i = -\Lambda_i\,y_i + \Lambda_i\,(H p)_i,\qquad \Lambda = \operatorname{diag}(4.77, 4.70, 15.5)\ \text{s}^{-1} \]
\[ H = \begin{pmatrix} -0.003 & -1.812 & -0.002\\ 1.823 & -0.002 & -1.813\\ -0.493 & -0.446 & -0.490 \end{pmatrix}\ \text{mm/psi} \]

Derivation (virtual work, Taylor expansion of the arc, substitution): M2 and Results §2. The derived structure fixes the form; every value is fitted. ndosmc.py:110-119, task_space_model.py:359

3State-space form

\[ \dot X = \begin{pmatrix} -\Lambda & \Lambda H\\ 0 & -\tfrac1\tau I \end{pmatrix} X + \begin{pmatrix} 0\\ \tfrac1\tau G \end{pmatrix} u(t - T),\qquad X = \begin{pmatrix} y\\ p \end{pmatrix},\quad y = \begin{pmatrix} I & 0 \end{pmatrix} X \]

M3

M2 with second-order mechanics, \(\ddot y_i + 2\zeta_i\omega_i\dot y_i + \omega_i^2 y_i = \omega_i^2 (Hp)_i\): \(\omega = 7.61, 7.87\) rad/s (1.2 Hz), \(\zeta = 0.73, 0.77\) (x, y). It fits no better than M2 at the tested frequencies, so no controller uses it.

F: frequency-identified per-axis model (used by the MPC)

1Two channels instead of three segments

\[ P^{\text{cmd}}_{S2} = 4.5 + \tfrac{\nu_y}{2},\qquad P^{\text{cmd}}_{S3} = 4.5 - \nu_x,\qquad P^{\text{cmd}}_{S4} = 4.5 - \tfrac{\nu_y}{2} \]

\(\nu_x, \nu_y\) (psi): channel commands; positive \(\nu\) moves the tip in the positive direction. No z control. mpc_controller.py:223-226, sysid_frf.py:133

2Stage A (actuator) and stage B (mechanics) per axis

\[ \frac{p_i(s)}{\nu_i(s)} = \frac{\gamma_i\,e^{-sT}}{\tau_i s + 1},\qquad \frac{y_x(s)}{p_x(s)} = \frac{0.1000}{s^2 + 10.30\,s + 56.06},\qquad \frac{y_y(s)}{p_y(s)} = \frac{0.0797\,s + 0.1350}{s^3 + 9.855\,s^2 + 61.09\,s + 74.68} \]

\(\gamma = (1.097, 1.142)\), \(\tau = 0.599\) s, \(T = 0.50\) s (x, y); outputs in m. Stage B poles: x \(-5.15 \pm 5.43j\); y \(-4.15 \pm 5.57j\), \(-1.55\). sysid_frf.py:588-608, 683-748; models/sysid_calibrated_v2.json

3Discrete state space

\[ \chi_{k+1} = A_d\,\chi_k + B_d\,\nu_{k-N},\qquad y_k = C\chi_k,\qquad \chi_1 = p \]

Stage B in controllable canonical form behind the lag state; ZOH at \(\Delta t\). sysid_frf.py:720-767, mpc_controller.py:75-79

All model-based controllers use only tip, tip velocity and pressure-sensor data, except the notebook SMC, whose \(k_n, c_n, b_n\) come from the simulator. Tip data carry 0.1 mm added noise in identification. Validation is free-run (multi-step) on seeds not used for fitting.

benchmark_slide_tasks.py:253 (score). RMSE = shape error + timing error, roughly: a controller can have a small shape error and a large RMSE (right path, late) or the reverse (on time, wrong size).

From a correction to three pressures

PD and the notebook SMC compute a planar correction \(\Delta p_{xy}\in\mathbb R^2\) and allocate it; the paper and delay-aware controllers invert an identified 3×3 matrix; the MPC uses the fixed channel map of model F.

\[ \Delta P_{S2..S4} = \mathcal D^{+}\Delta p_{xy},\qquad \mathcal D = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\phi_2 & \cos\phi_3 & \cos\phi_4\\ \sin\phi_2 & \sin\phi_3 & \sin\phi_4 \end{pmatrix} \]

\(\phi_j\): column azimuths; \(\mathcal D^{+}\): Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse (minimum-norm). The notebook used \((-\sin\phi_j, \cos\phi_j)\) instead, the bending-moment axis, which is \(\mathcal D\) rotated by 90°: each axis then drove the other. "Corrected allocator" = \(\mathcal D\). smc_reduced_model.py:104-111

PD

\[ \Delta p_{xy} = K_p\,(r_{xy} - \xi_{xy}) - K_d\,\dot\xi_{xy},\qquad K_p = 500\ \text{psi/m},\ K_d = 20\ \text{psi·s/m} \]

Absolute tip in metres; derivative on the measurement. No model, no delay compensation. smc_reduced_model.py:114-127

Notebook SMC (one-mode model)

1Sliding variable for a second-order model

\[ \sigma = \dot e + \lambda e \]

On \(\sigma = 0\): \(\dot e = -\lambda e\), so \(e\) decays at rate \(\lambda\).

2Differentiate along the model and impose the reaching law

\[ \dot\sigma = -k_n y - c_n\dot y + b_n\Delta p - \ddot r + \lambda\dot e \;\overset{!}{=}\; -K_s\,\operatorname{sat}(\sigma/\phi) \]

3Control law

\[ \Delta p = \frac{1}{b_n}\Big[k_n y + c_n\dot y + \ddot r - \lambda\dot e - K_s\operatorname{sat}(\sigma/\phi)\Big] \]

\(\dot r, \ddot r\): backward differences. Then allocate. smc_reduced_model.py:130-177

VariantAllocator\(y\)\(\lambda\) (s⁻¹)\(K_s\) (m/s²)\(\phi\) (m/s)
as writtennotebook (rotated)absolute50.20.02
λ = 8correcteddeviation \(\xi - \xi_0\)80.20.02
λ = 5, K = 0.35 (MPC script)correcteddeviation50.350.02

No delay, no lag, no gravity in the model, so it reacts to a tip that lags the commands by about 1.1 s; this keeps it slow and smaller than the reference (size 66–77 % on the scored circle).

Paper SMC and NDOSMC (M1)

1Sliding variable for a first-order model (paper eq. 4)

\[ \sigma_i = e_i = y_i - r_i \]

2SMC law (paper eq. 5)

\[ \dot\sigma_i = -a_iy_i + b_iv_i - \dot r_i \overset{!}{=} -\lambda\sigma_i - \eta_i\operatorname{sign}\sigma_i \;\Rightarrow\; v_i = \frac{1}{b_i}\big[\dot r_i + a_iy_i - \lambda\sigma_i - \eta_i\operatorname{sign}\sigma_i\big],\quad u = G_1^{-1}v \]
\[ \eta_i = \frac{\delta k_i|y_i| + \delta c_i|\dot y_i|}{|c_i|} + \epsilon \]

\(\delta k, \delta c\): spread of the identified \(k, c\) across set points. Gains \(\lambda = 1\), \(\epsilon = 0.1\). The paper's printed \(B = -1/c\) is replaced by \(+1/c\) (sign error). ndosmc.py:171-191

3Nonlinear disturbance observer (paper eqs. 6–9)

\[ \hat d_i = z_i + l_1 y_i + l_2 y_i|y_i|,\qquad \dot z_i = g_i\big(a_iy_i - b_iv_i - \hat d_i\big),\qquad g_i = l_1 + 2l_2|y_i| \]

Estimates the lumped \(d\) in \(\dot y_i = -a_iy_i + b_iv_i + d_i\). Eq. 7's sign corrected. ndosmc.py:194-215

4NDOSMC law (paper eqs. 12, 14)

\[ v_i = \frac{1}{b_i}\big[\dot r_i + a_iy_i - \lambda\sigma_i - \eta_i\operatorname{sat}(\sigma_i/\mu) - \hat d_i\big],\qquad \eta_i = \Phi e^{-g_it} + \epsilon/g_i \]

Gains \(\lambda = 1\), \(l_1 = 0.5\), \(l_2 = 0\), \(\mu = 0.1\) mm, \(\Phi = 1\), \(\epsilon = 1\). ndosmc.py:218-253

M1 does not contain the 0.5 s delay. The observer's \(\hat d\) is then mostly the controller's own input arriving 0.5 s late, so its correction comes late: NDOSMC is worse than SMC on the scored circle (2.84 vs 1.46 mm).

Delay-aware SMC (M2)

Paper SMC on M2, with a Smith predictor for \(T\) and a lag inverse for \(\tau\). Every step \(k\): ndosmc.py:284-312

1Model without the delay, driven by the commands actually sent

\[ \hat p_{k+1} = \hat p_k + \tfrac{\Delta t}{\tau}\big(G u_k - \hat p_k\big),\qquad \hat y_{k+1} = \hat y_k + \Delta t\big(-\Lambda\hat y_k + \Lambda H\hat p_k\big) \]

\(u_k\) is the clipped command. \(\hat y_k\) is the model's forecast of \(y_{k+N}\). lines 304-310

2Smith predictor (Smith 1957)

\[ \tilde y_k = \hat y_k + \big(y_k - \hat y_{k-N}\big) \approx y_{k+N} \]

\(\hat y_{k-N}\): model's estimate of \(y_k\); the bracket is the measured model error, assumed constant over \(T\). line 287

3Sliding variable on predicted quantities

\[ \sigma_k = \tilde y_k - \tilde r_k \]

Once \(\sigma \to 0\): \(y_{k+N} \approx \tilde r_k\), i.e. \(y(t) \approx \tilde r(t - T)\). For \(y(t) = r(t)\) the target must be \(\tilde r(t) = r(t + T)\) (next section).

4SMC law on M2 → desired pressure

\[ \dot{\tilde y} = -\Lambda\tilde y + \Lambda Hp,\quad \dot\sigma \overset{!}{=} -\lambda\sigma - \eta\operatorname{sat}(\sigma/\mu) \;\Rightarrow\; p_{\text{des}} = H^{-1}\Lambda^{-1}\big[\dot{\tilde r} + \Lambda\tilde y - \lambda\sigma - \eta\operatorname{sat}(\sigma/\mu)\big] \]

Gains \(\lambda = 8\) s⁻¹, \(\eta = 1\) mm/s, \(\mu = 1\) mm. lines 295-297 (via _law, 229-242)

5Lag inverse → command

\[ \tau\dot p = -p + Gu \;\Rightarrow\; u_k = G^{-1}\big(p_{\text{des},k} + \tau\,\dot p_{\text{des},k}\big),\qquad \dot p_{\text{des},k} = \frac{p_{\text{des},k} - p_{\text{des},k-1}}{\Delta t} \]

Then \(P^{\text{cmd}} = \operatorname{clip}(4.5 + u_k, 0, 9)\). At 0.4 Hz the lag inverse multiplies a sinusoid by \(|1 + i\omega\tau| = 1.81\), which is why commands reach the limits on fast motions. lines 298-302

6Optional: observer (delay-aware NDOSMC)

\[ p_{\text{des}} \to p_{\text{des}} - H^{-1}\Lambda^{-1}\hat d,\qquad \hat d \text{ from the NDOB with } y \to \tilde y \]

Gains \(\lambda = 4\), \(l_1 = 0.1\), \(\mu = 1\) mm, \(\Phi = 1\), \(\epsilon = 1\). Changes RMSE by ≤ 0.03 mm on the circles.

Three ways to get r(t + T)

The harness passes only \(r_k\). The delay-aware SMC needs \(\tilde r_k \approx r_{k+N}\); the MPC needs \(r\) over its whole horizon.

ATaylor estimate (delay-aware SMC default)

\[ \tilde r_k = r_k + T\dot r_k + \tfrac12T^2\ddot r_k,\qquad \dot{\tilde r}_k = \dot r_k + T\ddot r_k \]

For \(r = R e^{i\omega t}\): \(\tilde r = r(1 + i\omega T - \tfrac12\omega^2T^2)\) vs the true \(r\,e^{i\omega T}\). At 0.4 Hz (\(\omega T = 1.26\)): magnitude 1.27 at 80.5° instead of 1 at 72°, so the tip traces a circle 27 % too large; at 0.5 Hz, 1.59. At a triangle corner the estimate continues along the old edge, up to \(|v|T \approx 2\) mm past the corner. At 0.1 Hz (\(\omega T = 0.31\)) the error is 0.1 %. ndosmc.py:292-293

BExact future reference [diagnostic]

\[ \tilde r_k = r_{k+N} \]

Read from the trajectory's definition. Requires the trajectory in advance; the harness does not provide it. Used to measure what perfect preview is worth. ndosmc.py:289-290 (exact_preview=True); benchmark_slide_tasks.py:105 (Ahead)

CHistory-based predictor (RefPredictor, from the MPC)

\[ \text{before a period is found: } r_{j} = c + a_1 r_{j-1} + a_2 r_{j-2}\ \ (\text{LS on the last 4 s, every 0.1 s}),\ \text{iterated forward} \]
\[ P^* = \arg\min_{P}\ \tfrac{1}{200}\textstyle\sum_{m=0}^{199}\big(r_{k-m} - r_{k-m-P}\big)^2,\ \ P \in [1, 15]\ \text{s};\qquad \text{after: } \hat r_{k+n} = r_{k+n-P^*\lceil n/P^*\rceil} \]

A sampled sinusoid plus offset satisfies the AR(2) recursion exactly (\(a_1 = 2\cos\omega h\), \(a_2 = -1\)); period replay is exact for any periodic reference, corners included. A period is accepted when the matching error is below \(10^{-6}\) of the variance of the history; first possible after one period + 2 s. No knowledge of the trajectory is used. mpc_controller.py:132-191; benchmark_unified.py:85-107 (wrapper for the SMC)

Delay-compensated MPC

One controller per axis (x, y) on model F; no z control. mpc_controller.py:70-129, 194-226

1Kalman filter with a tip-offset state

\[ \begin{pmatrix}\hat\chi\\ \hat w\end{pmatrix} \leftarrow \begin{pmatrix}\hat\chi\\ \hat w\end{pmatrix} + L\left(\begin{pmatrix} y\\ p \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} C\hat\chi + \hat w\\ \hat\chi_1 \end{pmatrix}\right) \]

\(w\) (m): random-walk tip offset (drift, model error). \(L\): steady-state Kalman gain from the discrete Riccati equation with \(\sigma_\nu = 0.05\) psi, \(\sigma_w = 10^{-5}\) m, \(\sigma_{\text{tip}} = 10^{-4}\) m, \(\sigma_p = 2\cdot10^{-3}\) psi. Measuring \(p\) gives the lag state directly. lines 81-91, 118-129

2Predict across the delay

\[ \hat\chi_{k+N} = A_d^{N}\hat\chi_k + \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} A_d^{\,N-1-i}B_d\,\nu_{k-N+i} \]

The last \(N\) commands are already sent, so the state \(T\) ahead is known up to model error. Same role as the Smith predictor. lines 93-95

3Cost over the horizon \(H_p = 300\) steps (3 s)

\[ J = \sum_{n=1}^{H_p}\big(\hat y_{k+N+n} + \hat w - \hat r_{k+N+n-1}\big)^2 + R_u\sum_{n=0}^{H_p-1}\big(\nu_{k+n} - \nu_{k+n-1}\big)^2,\qquad R_u = 10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{psi}^2 \]

\(\hat r\): reference from RefPredictor (method C). \(R_u\) tuned on a different task (5 mm, 0.07 Hz, seed 5). lines 56-57, 97-112

4Closed-form minimiser, first move only

\[ \hat y = \Phi\hat\chi_{k+N} + \Gamma U,\quad \Phi_n = CA_d^{n},\ \Gamma_{nm} = CA_d^{n-m-1}B_d\ (m < n) \]
\[ U^* = \big(\Gamma^\top\Gamma + R_uD^\top D\big)^{-1}\big[\Gamma^\top(\hat r - \Phi\hat\chi_{k+N} - \hat w\mathbf 1) + R_uD^\top e_1\nu_{k-1}\big],\qquad \nu_k = U^*_1 \]

\(U = (\nu_k, \dots, \nu_{k+H_p-1})\); \(D\): first-difference matrix. Unconstrained: the 0–9 psi limits are applied by clipping afterwards, and the clipped value is fed back to the filter. The first row of the inverse is precomputed, so each step is four dot products. lines 97-112, 223-226

Differences from the delay-aware SMC: a higher-order model (F vs M2), an optimised command over 3 s instead of a sliding law, the history-based reference predictor by default, no z control.

Results

156 runs: 12 controllers × 13 tests, one harness loop, same metrics. Gains as stated above, not retuned per test. ★ and bold: best non-diagnostic controller in each column. [diag]: sees the true future reference, not available to a real controller.

uv run python scripts/benchmark_unified.py --workers 10; every run's gains, seed and metrics in docs/figures/benchmark_unified.json. Sanity checks passed: reproduces compare_controllers.py, mpc_controller.py (1.220 mm), motion_tests.py and benchmark_slide_tasks.py (230 comparisons, largest difference 9·10⁻¹⁶).

What the numbers show

  • Modelling the delay and lag is what matters. On the scored circle after the first lap: PD 3.96, notebook SMC 1.98–4.08, paper SMC (M1, no delay) 0.87, delay-aware SMC 0.09, MPC 0.057 mm.
  • The predicted reference decides fast and cornered motions. On the brief tasks (except the unreachable 8.9 mm circle), the delay-aware SMC traces paths 128–210 % of the reference size with the Taylor estimate, 102–123 % with the history-based predictor and 103–125 % with the exact future [diag].
  • On the synthetic tests the two controllers with the history-based predictor are best. Delay-aware SMC + RefPredictor has ★ in 6 columns (scored circle 0.034, axial x 0.034, brief axial, ellipse, 8.9 mm circle, held-out tie), the MPC in 5 (triangles 0.62 and 0.71, axial y 0.011, fast circle 0.15, held-out tie). The MPC is ahead wherever corners or 0.4 Hz make the first lap hard.
  • On the recorded robot runs the delay-aware SMC/NDOSMC with the Taylor estimate is best (1.06–1.64 mm), and the MPC is worst of the predictive controllers (3.1–4.5 mm). The recorded paths never repeat exactly, so no period is detected (0 of 18 000 steps) and the predictor stays on AR(2).
  • Triangles hurt predictor C before the period is found: AR(2) cannot predict corners, and the delay-aware SMC + RefPredictor saturates 40–54 % of the time during the first lap (4.05 mm RMS over 10–12.5 s, then 0.14 mm over 15–30 s).
  • Nikoletta's SMC draws the right shape late. Its shape error is small on the axial and slow tests (0.01–0.02 mm on MT axial), but it lags 0.3–0.7 s, so its RMSE is large.
  • Reach limits tie everyone. On the 10 mm held-out circle every predictive controller scores 0.92–0.97 mm with 19–21 % saturation; on the 8.9 mm 0.4 Hz circle 2.2–2.4 mm with 26–81 %.
